claim_boundary: This artifact records an operational and mathematical decomposition assessment for numeric computation scheduling. It is not a theorem-level invariant certificate.

mathematical_decomposition.current_outer_chunk: A chunk is one fixed component-label sector.
mathematical_decomposition.current_inner_formula: For each fixed sector, braid_quantum_trace sums dimension(total_charge) times the trace of the braid action over the fusion path basis for that total charge.
mathematical_decomposition.exact_first_split: Split a fixed sector by total_charge. The sector trace is the sum over total_charge partial traces, so these microchunks can be computed independently and aggregated by addition.
mathematical_decomposition.exact_second_split: For a fixed sector and total_charge, split the trace by initial basis path blocks. The trace is the sum of diagonal matrix coefficients, so disjoint initial-basis blocks can be computed independently and aggregated by addition.
mathematical_decomposition.framing_and_coefficient: Apply the fixed-sector framing factor and untwisted coefficient either once in the final sector aggregator or consistently to each microchunk with documented normalization.

assessment.reason: Whole-sector singleton scheduling has no checkpoint inside expensive sectors. Easy sectors are already mostly exhausted, and remaining/missing sectors include large basis/state-size sectors where one sector can occupy a worker for hours.
expected_benefits: turn multi-hour invisible sector jobs into smaller interruptible jobs
reduce lost work from killed workers or remote shutdown
make Linux/Mac cross-validation cheaper at the microchunk level
allow worker pools to rebalance hard sectors instead of waiting behind a single long sector
main_risks: floating summation order changes; aggregator must use a fixed order and tolerance
current compose_sparse starts from the full identity on the total-charge basis; path-block mode needs a restricted-column implementation to avoid doing the same full work repeatedly
microchunk artifacts need a new schema and validation against already completed whole-sector chunks

recommended_next_steps: Implement a microchunk evaluator mode for sector_index plus total_charge.
Validate total-charge aggregation against several already completed whole-sector chunks, including fast, medium, and hard examples.
If total-charge chunks remain too large, implement restricted initial-basis block mode so each microchunk propagates only selected source columns.
Only after validation, stop or drain current long workers and requeue remaining work as microchunks.
